label: Eco tip of the day
items: Carry a reusable bottle: one refillable bottle can replace hundreds of single-use ones a year.
Unplug devices that sit on standby; chargers and TVs sip power all day.
Wash clothes in cold water; most of the energy is spent on heating the water.
Compost food scraps: in landfill they make methane, a powerful greenhouse gas.
Rinse and drain recyclables; food residue can spoil a whole load.
Keep a reusable bag by the door so it is there when you need it.
Take a bag on your walk and pick up ten pieces of litter. Wear gloves and avoid anything sharp or hazardous.
Return plastic bags and film to store drop-off bins; they jam curbside sorting machines.
Lower the thermostat one or two degrees and add a sweater.
Fix dripping taps: a drip can waste thousands of litres a year.
Repair before you replace; a repair cafe can fix electronics and clothes.
Buy loose fruit and vegetables and skip the plastic bags.
Switch old bulbs to LED: about 75-80% less energy and they last far longer.
Meatless meals a few days a week reduce your food footprint quickly.
Plan meals to avoid food waste; the best scrap is the one never created.
Batteries and electronics never go in the garbage or recycling; use a drop-off depot.
Choose products with less packaging, or in glass, metal or paper.
Shorter showers save water and the energy used to heat it.
Close the fridge door quickly and keep the coils clean for better efficiency.
Walk, cycle or take transit for one trip this week.
Second-hand first: clothes, furniture and tools often last longer than new ones.
Plant something: even a pot of herbs helps pollinators and reduces packaging.
Pizza boxes with grease belong in compost, not recycling.
Join a local cleanup. Shoreline litter is easier to remove before it breaks into microplastics.
Use a lid when cooking: it saves energy and speeds up dinner.
Air-dry a load of laundry instead of using the dryer.
Choose a refillable cleaning product and keep the bottle.
Share rides, tools and ideas; sharing cuts cost and waste.
Check your recycling rules each year; they change.
Small habits, repeated, beat one big gesture. Pick one today.
